source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.teacher_note: The even expression rule also covers this: {'excluded_case': 'Do not assume x^2 + 2 is always even just because the added constant is even.', 'reason', so it is not an exception — on the item about Can I decide whether an arithmetic or algebraic.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: even expression is settled by running 'Can I keep the direction of a divisibility claim straight when adding': If a divides M and a divides N, then a divides M + N and M - N. The reverse direction is — on the item about Can I decide whether an arithmetic or algebraic.

intelligence.enrichment: An expression is always even when every possible value can be written as 2 times an integer, such as 4m + 2q = 2(2m + q). An expression like x^2 + 2 is not always even because x^2 has the same parity as x.
